bug_semantics: A same-tenant attacker can create a chat-link session for an attacker-controlled Slack, Discord, Teams, or Telegram identity and induce a logged-in victim to complete the handoff. In the advisory's POST form, the public GET renders the session's confirmationToken into HTML and the public POST accepts that token while deriving globalUserId from the victim's authenticated browser session; because the chat-link session is not bound to the Budibase user who prepared it, the attacker-controlled external identity is persisted against the victim's global user ID and can invoke agent operations with the victim's permissions.
flaw_origin: Commit 6fdd3bb496d0b648f4969a8a5c505dee477a022f first introduced the complete flawed trust boundary: an external chat user could mint an identity-link session, publicRoutes exposed its handoff URL, and handoffChatLinkSession consumed the externally created session and called upsertChatIdentityLink with the currently authenticated browser user's globalUserId without any requester/user binding. Commit 02d32c2cc0fd19584c63e5f6f9030a82a7b18b7a later added the plaintext confirmationToken and POST consent layer described by the advisory, but it preserved rather than originated the cross-user binding flaw.
ai_marker: absent: the raw BIC commit object names author Peter Clement <peterclmnt@gmail.com> and committer Peter Clement <peterclmnt@gmail.com>; its message is 'Authenticate agent channel deployment with budibase' and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/security/advisories/GHSA-pvcr-8mvp-w8qr identifies the public GET/POST /api/chat-links/:instance/:token/handoff flow, packages/server/src/api/routes/chat.ts, packages/server/src/api/controllers/ai/chatIdentityLinks.ts, packages/server/src/sdk/workspace/ai/chatIdentityLinks.ts, the HTML-hidden confirmationToken, the missing requester binding, and patched version 3.40.0; the assigned alias is https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4q4m-8h83-fcmr. In full history, git log -L over the vulnerable confirmation/upsert handler and git log -S'globalUserId: currentGlobalUserId' trace the causal binding statements to 6fdd3bb496d0b648f4969a8a5c505dee477a022f, while git log -S'confirmationToken' traces only the later consent wrapper to 02d32c2cc0fd19584c63e5f6f9030a82a7b18b7a. At the BIC, packages/server/src/api/controllers/webhook/chatHandler.ts:441 creates the session from the external chat identity; packages/server/src/api/routes/chat.ts:22-25 installs the public GET; packages/server/src/api/controllers/ai/chatIdentityLinks.ts:39-86 takes ctx's currentGlobalUserId and writes it at lines 75-83 together with the session's external identity; packages/server/src/sdk/workspace/ai/chatIdentityLinks.ts:351-397 creates the token/session without a Budibase user binding and lines 436 onward performs the identity-link upsert. Direct-parent tree verification with git diff --name-status 5ef9a4f17ffc7ff25bac8c75ab1485b01586b889 6fdd3bb496d0b648f4969a8a5c505dee477a022f shows the controller and SDK files added and the route file modified; the parent's packages/server/src/api/routes/chat.ts has no chat-link route, and the two newly added files do not exist there. The first-party feature PR https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/pull/18293 lists 6fdd3bb496d0b648f4969a8a5c505dee477a022f as its first ordinary member commit with direct parent 5ef9a4f17ffc7ff25bac8c75ab1485b01586b889, so no squash decomposition is needed. Version-tree checks show tag 3.34.1 lacks the route and binding, tag 3.34.2 contains publicRoutes.get and globalUserId: currentGlobalUserId, tag 3.39.29 still lacks confirmationGlobalUserId, and tag 3.39.30 contains the user-binding checks; both the direct fix and landed merge are also contained by 3.40.0. Thus the source-history boundary is first affected 3.34.2 and first fixed 3.39.30, although the advisory conservatively declares all versions <3.40.0 affected and 3.40.0 patched. First-party fix PR https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/pull/19194 is titled 'Bind chat identity link confirmation to the current user' and names the advisory; direct commit https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/commit/e2aa86793bbf4771f38b89a70ebb0a72b81af83b stores confirmationGlobalUserId during preparation and rejects a confirmer whose currentGlobalUserId differs, and merge commit https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/commit/362e6c654fb4da6e123c734333da2d6cbdcdb7ef lands PR #19194. Exact AI attribution was checked only on the BIC via numactl --cpunodebind=1 --membind=1 git cat-file -p 6fdd3bb496d0b648f4969a8a5c505dee477a022f, yielding human author/committer identities and no trailers.
reasoning: The vulnerability is not merely that a confirmation token appeared in HTML; its causal invariant is that a session created for one external identity can be consumed in another person's authenticated Budibase browser and the consumer's globalUserId becomes the link target. The earliest commit that created that invariant is 6fdd3bb496d0b648f4969a8a5c505dee477a022f: its public GET performed the link immediately, so a victim opening an attacker-generated handoff URL was already sufficient. The later 02d32c2cc0fd19584c63e5f6f9030a82a7b18b7a changed the trigger into the advisory's GET-page/POST-token consent sequence, but its parent already had the same cross-user identity-confusion outcome and its unchanged binding lines trace back to 6fdd3bb496d0b648f4969a8a5c505dee477a022f; it is therefore not the BIC. The direct parent of 6fdd3bb496d0b648f4969a8a5c505dee477a022f has neither the linking controller nor SDK and has no public chat-link route, proving vulnerable-line absence. Direct fix e2aa86793bbf4771f38b89a70ebb0a72b81af83b adds the missing user/session binding and equality check, and 362e6c654fb4da6e123c734333da2d6cbdcdb7ef lands that first-party fix. Release trees corroborate introduction before the affected range and remediation no later than the advisory's 3.40.0 boundary. Because the BIC's commit object is an ordinary human-authored commit with no AI marker, the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
